'''Karl Friedrich August Gutzmer''' (2 February 1860 – 10 May 1924) was a German [[mathematician]] who was chairman of some German commissions about improvement of the teaching of mathematics.{{sfn | Klein | 2016 | p=295 }}

== Life and work ==
Gutzmer was born near [[Schwerin]] but his family moved to Berlin when he was eight years old. In Berlin he studied in ''Friedrichswerdersche Gymnasium'' till 1881.{{sfn | Malonek | Kharlamova | 2010 | p=63 }} From 1881 to 1884 he attended mathematics lectures at [[Berlin University]] despite not being registered as a student.{{sfn | Schmerling | 1998 | p=Levensdaten }} He graduated in 1887 in Berlin.

He began his academic career publishing five articles in the Portuguese journal ''Jornal de Sciencias mathematicas e astronomicas'' (best known as ''Teixeira's Journal'') between 1887 and 1890.{{sfn | Malonek | Kharlamova | 2010 | p=64 }} In 1893 he was awarded a doctorate submitting at the [[University of Halle]] a dissertation about certain partial differential equations. Married in the same year, he left his academic career to manage his wife's lands.{{sfn | Schmerling | 1998 | p=Levensdaten }} In 1894 he returned to teaching at the [[Technische Hochschule]] in Charlottenburg (now [[Technische Universität Berlin]]) and the following year he obtained his ''venia legendi'' at the University of Halle where he taught as assistant professor till 1899.{{sfn | Malonek | Kharlamova | 2010 | p=65 }}

From 1900 to 1905 he was full professor at the [[University of Jena]]. In 1905 he returned to Halle University succeeding [[Georg Cantor]],{{sfn | Malonek | Kharlamova | 2010 | p=66 }} where he remained till his death in 1924. He was rector of the university (1914–1915), chairman of the German Committee for Mathematical and Scientific Teaching (1908–1913), member of the [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] from 1900 and his president from 1922 to 1924.{{sfn | Schmerling | 1998 | p=Levensdaten }} At the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] he was an invited speaker in 1904 in Heidelberg<ref>{{cite book|chapter=''Über die auf die Anwendungen gerichteten Bestrebungen im mathematischen Unterricht der deutschen Universitäten'' von A. Gutzmer|pages=586–593|title=Verhandlungen des dritten internationalen Mathematiker-Kongresses in Heidelberg von 8. bis 13. August 1904|location=Leipzig|publisher=B. G. Teubner|year=1905|chapter-url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=miun.aag4063.0004.001&view=1up&seq=604}}</ref> and in 1908 in Rome.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Daum|title=Wissenschaftspopularisierung|pages=367, 389, 489, including a short biography}}</ref>

Gutzmer published more than forty works; among them, the reports about the activities of the teaching committee are specially relevant. He also wrote a history of the [[German Mathematical Society]].{{sfn | Schmerling | 1998 | p=Schriften }}
